summary: MCP discovery, read, validation, search, record evidence, and contract-manifest tools.

tools.display_name: Workspace Chassis Control Engine admission runtime diagnostic
tools.notes: Read-only agent-safe MCP route that diagnoses the running MCP server process (not the caller shell) for Chassis Control Engine worker_admission_v1 runtime config. Reports only source names and booleans (service URL, API key, worker-admission route, request-contract digest presence, and whether the remote-admission observability path is loaded); never returns any secret value, route value, digest, key hash, bearer material, project id, or request/response body.

Compact daily-use MCP discovery surface for bounded catalog scans. Defaults to the first 20 compact entries and supports task_id, tool_name, and limit filters so agents do not pull the full catalog into context by accident. Use workspace_tools_describe for targeted per-tool detail and workspace_tools_query for filtered task_id/tool_name lookups; full descriptor fields remain available through explicit verbose/detail flows.

Targeted MCP detail surface for a known tool_name or a narrow filtered set; compact by default, pass verbose:true for the full descriptor fields. For routine bounded catalog browsing prefer the compact workspace_tools_list; for a known task_id/tool_name lookup use workspace_tools_query. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- tools-describe --json`.

Filtered MCP lookup for a known task_id or exact tool_name; already bounded, so it returns full entries by default (pass verbose:false for compact). For routine bounded catalog browsing prefer workspace_tools_list; for targeted per-tool detail use workspace_tools_describe. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- tools-describe --task <task_id>|--tool <tool_name> --json`.

Read-only agent-safe MCP route for byte-range reads from server-side response content references. Oversized tool results spill the complete JSON payload to the wiki-mcp runtime state directory and return a bounded preview plus a ref_id; callers use this tool with offset and length, base64-decode each data_base64 range, and concatenate bytes to reassemble the complete payload losslessly without carrying an oversized stdio frame.

Read-only MCP route that returns the shared wiki contract manifest (conventions, lint, schema, taxonomy, retrieval, query, and template references) from the checked-in contract tree. Takes no caller arguments and no caller-supplied filesystem root; the manifest is provenance/reference data, not authority to act.

Read-only introspection for the dispatch caller/session identity and bootstrap review contract. Identity authority must be launcher- or transport-minted; caller-supplied role identity is refused. Reports the current bootstrap state (bootstrap_exception_active / bootstrap_review_missing / bootstrap_exception_consumed). workspace_agent_dispatch is the active supported MCP dispatch surface.

paid_cce.notes: Read-only introspection for the dispatch caller/session identity and bootstrap review contract. Identity authority must be launcher- or transport-minted; caller-supplied role identity is refused. Reports the current bootstrap state (bootstrap_exception_active / bootstrap_review_missing / bootstrap_exception_consumed), and under a valid paid/CCE key posture the graph_impact_persistence_unavailable state for graph-impact evidence persistence prerequisites. workspace_agent_dispatch is the active supported MCP dispatch surface.

tools.notes: Preferred MCP search surface for repo-scoped wiki and docs lookup; compact and preview-oriented by default. For a full page or canonical record body use workspace_read_page or workspace_get_record instead. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- search --query <query> --json`.

Write-capable MCP route that builds or refreshes the lexical wiki/docs search index for a configured workspace repository — the explicit index-builder companion to workspace_search_repo. Pass reindex:true for a full rebuild. Resolves the repository through configured aliases and accepts no caller-supplied filesystem root. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- build-search-index`.

Preferred MCP page-read surface for repo-relative markdown paths and canonical JSON records; compact by default (omits body/raw), widened with include_body, include_raw, include_record, or verbose. For tracker WK-level reads, detailed done/cancelled/parked slice bodies and WK-level agent note bodies are intentionally omitted; counts, omission metadata, and agent_notes_bytes on included slice rows remain available. Use selected_slice:<slice-id> to read that slice's notes and agent_notes_bytes; full/debug opt-ins can retrieve complete detail and may spill. Graph-evidence sidecars at wiki/work-records/evidence/WK-####.graph.json are readable through this same tool (compact format `graph-evidence-sidecar`) and are replay/debug data, never dispatch authority: pass selected_slice:<slice-id> for one slice's replay entry, selected_record:true for only the record-level entry, or include_record/verbose for the full sidecar. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- read --path <repo-relative-path> --json`.

Preferred MCP canonical-record read surface for durable work-graph IDs; compact by default (omits the full record object and raw JSON), widened with include_record, include_raw, or verbose, and include_body for markdown records. For tracker work-record-level reads, detailed done/cancelled/parked slice bodies and work-record-level agent note bodies are intentionally omitted; counts, omission metadata, and agent_notes_bytes on included slice rows remain available. Use selected_slice:<slice-id> for that slice's notes and agent_notes_bytes; full/debug opt-ins can retrieve complete detail and may spill. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- get-record --id <work-graph-id|area-slug> --json`.

Preferred MCP dispatch-readiness surface for a WK or slice; read-only, returns the structured readiness envelope without touching the record. Compact by default (decision code, bounded reasons, next action); verbose:true restores the full envelope. Free/local readiness covers only the structural runnability floor (write_scope, acceptance, validation present, a supported role, a resolvable subject, a fresh source digest). Per DEC-0123/DEC-0125 a confirmed no-Node-Engine posture renders no local admissibility judgment, so admissibility threshold analysis is not part of free-tier readiness guidance. CLI fallback is operator-only.

paid_cce.notes: Preferred MCP dispatch-readiness surface for a WK or slice; read-only, returns the structured readiness envelope without touching the record. Compact by default (decision code, bounded reasons, next action); verbose:true restores the full envelope. Under a valid paid/CCE key posture the readiness envelope also carries Node-Engine-returned admissibility detail: blast-radius level, cluster count, and the CCE verdict/reason codes and recovery. These are NE-returned judgments and are reported as such, distinguished from the raw measured carrier facts the local layer forwards; the local layer renders no threshold verdict of its own (DEC-0125). Set node_engine_admissibility:true to evaluate CCE-exclusive implementation admissibility for a structurally dispatchable unit; only the CCE pack path can return an admit and there is no local admit fallback. CLI fallback is operator-only.

tools.notes: Agent-safe MCP route for persisting graph-impact derived evidence onto a WK or slice. Resolves the workspace through configured aliases; rejects caller-supplied filesystem roots and shell output as authority. The graph_impact payload must be an envelope produced by the workspace code-index graph-impact surface (graph_impact_paths or graph_impact_diff), and the persisted entry is validated against the work-record schema before writing. Compact by default; verbose:true for raw graph_state and full derived evidence.

Agent-safe MCP route for recording bounded review-attestation evidence onto a WK or slice after a trusted findings-only reviewer or redteam run. Binds the selected unit to the canonical record and source_digest and derives review facts from launcher/backend-minted run status, not caller prose, shell output, or raw final_result bodies. Records evidence only: it does not write accepted_authorities[], does not locally convert needs_review to admit, and does not replace Chassis Control Engine admission-time review validation.

Write-capable agent-safe MCP route that regenerates the non-canonical wiki views and then lints the configured workspace repository; use after structural wiki changes. Optional max_findings bounds returned findings (omit for the compact default, 0 for counts only, or a positive integer with no hard upper bound; large caps can produce large responses). The set-status/set-closure review/done transitions run this path automatically and surface its result as an advisory closeout_lint summary. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- generate-and-lint`.

Read-only agent-safe MCP route that validates a configured workspace repository against the shared wiki contract without writing views, caches, or records; use workspace_generate_and_lint when views must be refreshed first. Optional max_findings bounds returned findings (omit for the compact default, 0 for counts only, or a positive integer with no hard upper bound; large caps can produce large responses).

Explicit opt-in MCP route for repairing only missing docs backlink comments in canonical docs pages. It is separate from read-only workspace_lint_repo and from workspace_generate_and_lint, which remain non-autofixing. The route recomputes fresh lint findings internally, only applies structured missing_docs_backlink findings after docs-root revalidation, and never accepts caller-supplied findings as write authority; optional path/id/comment inputs are narrowing filters only.

Structured docs-policy validator that detects agent-facing non-MCP role-dispatch authority drift; operator/internal sections classified by heading are audience-scoped and do not automatically fail. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- docs-policy validate --json`.

Read-only agent FAQ served from the agent-faq.v1 known-issues corpus; each entry pairs a recurring symptom and cause with the exact structured workspace_* route(s) to resolve it and the responsible actor (agent vs operator). Returns all entries by default; pass id for one entry or related_code to filter by a runtime-blocker code. Output is tier-projected: free/local responses show only source-available coordination routes and omit paid/CCE remediation routes and next actions, which appear only under a valid paid/CCE key posture. Accepts no caller-supplied filesystem root. CLI fallback is operator-only.

Agent-safe MCP route for recording coordination-only review-result evidence onto a WK or slice when a trusted reviewer or redteam run yields `changes_requested` role-result evidence or structured missing-result/runtime-failure evidence. Keeps this surface distinct from accepted/no-findings review attestation and from completion-satisfying review evidence. Binds the selected unit to the canonical record and source_digest and derives facts from launcher/backend-minted run status, not caller prose, shell output, or raw final_result bodies. Records evidence only: it does not write accepted_authorities[], does not locally convert needs_review to admit, and does not replace Chassis Control Engine admission-time review validation.

Agent-safe MCP route for workers to run declared Node test validation for an implementation unit without raw shell or raw exec. Side effect: process_spawn. Caller input is exactly { unit, target } for the fixed enum command `node_test`; the handler loads the canonical work record/slice for `unit` itself and authorizes `target` solely from that unit's sections.structured_validation.allowed[] entries with command node_test. It then runs `node --check <target>` and, only if check passes, `node --test <target>` using argv arrays with shell:false. Node binary, cwd, env, per-step timeout, and output caps are internal server constants; caller-supplied authority-shaped fields (snapshot, runtime/env policy, node binary, cwd/workspace root, timeout, output cap, source digest, extra args) are rejected. Target must be repo-relative, canonical, existing, .js/.mjs, contained under the workspace repo, and not a symlink escape. Returns structured per-step evidence with node --test reported as skipped when node --check fails. Family-neutral: Codex, Claude, and Agy workers see the same contract. The structured evidence is command-surface validation, not a paid Chassis Control Engine enforcement attestation; arbitrary-command, npm-script, and cross-repo validation remain follow-up scope.
